survey: A three-masted wooden sailing ship floating in stylized waves, seen in a gentle three-quarter view from a little above. The bow with its curled prow is at the left and slightly nearer the viewer. The stern and its railing are at the right, a little farther away. Hull: the planks run along the side and curve up toward the bow. Three brass-rimmed portholes sit in a row along the side, which faces the camera almost head-on, so drawing them as near-circles is right. Deck and rails: from this viewpoint the tops of the rails and a little of the deck behind them show, and the far stern rail rises behind. Masts: the foremast, mainmast and mizzen stand vertical and parallel. The part of each mast above its sail lines up with the part below it at the deck, and each base passes down behind the rail. Each mast has a crow's-nest ring, a horizontal yard with rope ties and a small flag on top. Sails: the billowing sails hang from roughly horizontal yards. The foremast sail overlaps the mainsail and the mainsail overlaps the mizzen sail, which fits the bow being nearer. Rigging: ropes run from the yards and sail corners down to the rails at believable angles. Contact: the hull sits down in the water, the waves wrap around the waterline, and the spray at the bow matches the sea's level horizon.
